flagged.comment: No dumpster or central trash enclosure location is shown on either the site plan (Sheet 9) or the landscape plan (Sheet 31). The site plan contains only a note stating that trash containers shall not be left at curbside unattended; there is no graphic depiction of a designated dumpster location for consistency checking between plan sheets.

Dumpster/trash enclosure location is not shown on the site plan or landscape plan. Trash Collection Notes appear on Sheet 9 but no actual dumpster location or trash enclosure is depicted graphically. This prevents verification of consistency between sheets and compliance with waste management requirements.

Light pole and streetlight fixture locations and quantities are not called out on the landscape plan or other plan sheets. No light pole locations or fixture counts can be verified from the submitted materials.

Light pole and streetlight fixture locations are not marked or shown on the site plan or landscape plan. A lighting note and Figure 34 (fixture types) appear on Sheet 9, but actual fixture locations and quantities are not depicted, preventing verification of consistency between the landscape and site plans.

Acreage discrepancy exists between sheets. Cover sheet (Sheet 1) shows 'Project Area: 2.16 Acres,' while the site data table on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 'Site Area: 2.162 acres.' Although the difference is minor (0.002 acres), the values are not exactly consistent across plan sheets.

Acreage values are inconsistent across sheets. Cover sheet states 2.16 acres; Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows 94,192 sf (2.162 acres). These values do not match. Acreage must be consistent across all site plan sheets and the cover sheet.

Site measurements (lot dimensions/perimeter distances) are not shown on the site plan. While site area (94,192 sq ft / 2.162 acres) is provided and legal description is referenced, specific property line dimensions, bearings, and distances required by BCM 1.2.7 are not called out on the plan sheets.

Site measurements (lot dimensions including bearings and distances) are not shown on the main site plan (Sheet 9). While the Plat (Sheet 2) shows boundary bearings and distances, these critical measurements are not visible on the site plan as required by BCM 1.2.7.

Two perpetual recorded easements are not depicted on the submitted site plan: (1) Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731, 0.31 acres, NE interior of Lot 1) and (2) City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137, 0.130 acres, NE corner of Lot 1). These easements together encumber approximately 0.44 acres (~19% of the site) and are required to be depicted before plan approval. The Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) shows some easements labeled but does not show these two critical perpetual easements. All site plan and utility sheets must include depictions of these recorded easements.

Master Comment Report (LDE1) identifies that a License Agreement is required for the existing remaining concrete retaining wall adjacent to the street/ROW. The plans do not show callout with recorded document number or space for the license agreement reference, indicating this required legal instrument may not yet be executed and recorded with Travis County.

Drainage pattern delineation is not confirmed on the ESCP plan sheets. ECM 1.4.4.B.3 requires ESCP sheets to include existing conditions and drainage pattern delineation; however, specific drainage pattern arrows, flow direction indicators, or drainage area boundaries cannot be verified from the ESCP materials provided.

Above-grade features affecting drainage patterns (buildings, retaining walls, utility infrastructure) are depicted on ESCP and site plan sheets; however, the depiction of how the two perpetual easement areas (Greenbelt and Drainage) relate to drainage infrastructure and grading cannot be fully verified without these easement boundaries being shown. The relationship between proposed grading, drainage design, and the easement constraints must be clearly demonstrated.

Recorded easement document numbers are called out inconsistently across plan sheets. The Greenbelt Access & Use Easement is referenced as 'Doc. 2010070731' on Sheet 9 but 'Doc. 2010040121' on Sheet 11. The recorded instrument per county records is 2010070731. Sheet 11 contains an incorrect or conflicting document reference that must be corrected to ensure clear and accurate callout of the easement record number.

Travis County recorded document numbers are not clearly called out on the grading plan. Multiple easements are labeled with blank document number placeholders instead of actual recorded numbers: 'Wastewater Easement Doc#______', 'Sidewalk Easement Doc#______' (appears three times), and '10' Water Line Valve Easement Doc#______'. Actual document numbers must be provided.

Required record reference shown as blank placeholder. The cover sheet includes a note for the Integrated Pest Management Plan with a blank space for the Travis County document number: 'For Integrated Pest Management Plan, see agreement filed in document No. ___________, Official Public Records, Travis County, Texas.' The document number must be filled in with the actual recorded instrument number rather than left blank.

Required record references are shown as placeholder blanks rather than actual recorded document numbers. Sheet 11 depicts multiple easements with blank callouts (Doc#______) that should contain Travis County recorded instrument numbers. Provide the actual recorded document numbers for all easements shown on the plan.

Cannot verify that Sheet 18 (Austin Water General Information & Construction Notes) independently includes the engineer's dated signature, seal, firm name, and Texas PE registration number on the sheet itself. UCM 2.5.1.E.1 requires these elements on each utility plan sheet; however, the title block and certification elements for Sheet 18 cannot be confirmed from available materials.

Utility plan sheets contain inconsistent and outdated PE seal information. Professional Engineer Jason K. Rodgers' Texas PE license number is inconsistent across sheets: Sheet 18 shows 87881, Sheet 19 shows 97861, Sheet 20 shows 97861, and Sheet 21 shows 87821. Additionally, seal dates on Sheets 19-21 are significantly outdated (2020-2023) compared to Sheet 18 (2-27-25). All utility sheets must be sealed by the same engineer with consistent license number and current dated signatures.

Streetscape elements (curb lines, parking layout, parking stripes, parking garage entrance, light pole locations) are not confirmed as matching between the landscape plan and site plan. Both sheets show consistent site layout, but specific streetscape element callouts cannot be verified on both sheets independently.

Proposed land use shown as 'Multi-Family Residential' with 39 townhome units is consistent across site plan sheets reviewed; however, consistency with all required application documents (site data table, building data table, parking calculation table, building summary table, project application, TIA Determination Worksheet, Austin Fire Department intended use table, and engineering summary letter) cannot be verified without detailed review of all supplementary documents and their use designation tables.

Site area calculations contain discrepancies. Cover sheet shows 2.16 acres; Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows 94,192 sf, which calculates to 2.162 acres. Additionally, facts.md notes COA GIS measures the parcel at 2.111 acres (91,944 sf). Site area accuracy cannot be verified due to these variations.

Adjacent properties (LOT 2 MECEY SUBDIVISION, LOT A CORTEZ HEIGHTS, and others) are shown on multiple plan sheets for context, but cannot be confirmed as grayed out or distinguishable with SP numbers. Representation of adjacent sites cannot be verified from available materials.

While topography, existing structures, and drainage patterns are generally shown on the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) and ESCP (Sheet 5), the two perpetual easements (Greenbelt Access and City of Austin Drainage) that affect existing site conditions are not labeled or depicted on these sheets. These must be shown and labeled as existing recorded encumbrances affecting the permitted site boundary.

Site plan does not include a callout identifying the existing concrete retaining wall in the ROW requiring a license agreement, nor does it provide space for the license agreement recordation number. Per Code of Ordinances § 14-11-41 and LDE1 comments, the plan sheet must identify this element and include space for the recorded document number.

Cannot verify that the current version of the Austin Water General Information and Construction Notes Sheet is included in the plan set. UCM 2.5.1.E.22 requires the current version; however, the version date or publication date of Sheet 18 cannot be confirmed from available materials.
